public_body: Chatham Affordable Housing Trust Fund Board Of Trustees
overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair lawfully exercised his §20(g) discretion by polling the board and following its majority, and the Act does not require public speaking opportunities.

allegations.summary: Alleged the chair failed to use his own G.L. c. 30A, §20(g) authority to permit a non-resident to speak, and instead let the full board vote on it, denying the speaker.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, by choosing to ask for input from fellow Board members and choosing to follow the wishes of the majority of the Board, even if they were not his own personal wishes, Chair Schell exercised his authority and discretion as chair to determine who may speak or otherwise participate at a meeting.

allegations.summary: Alleged other board members violated the law by failing to object when the chair sought to confirm the earlier vote, and by confirming their own prior votes.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that members of the public be provided an opportunity to speak during meetings of public bodies.
